distractors.reason: We don't say 'watch a bus'. 'Watch' is used with things you look at, such as a film or a match.
We don't say 'hold a bus'. 'Hold' means keep something in your hands or in a position.
We don't say 'open a bus'. 'Open' is used with doors, windows or shops.

example_sentence: I have to ___ a bus to the station at eight o'clock.
l1_interference: Polacy często używają 'take' we wszystkich zwrotach z 'brać' lub 'łapać', ale w angielskim do autobusu naturalnie pasuje 'catch', bo to czasownik oznaczający zdążenie na pojazd.
explanation: In English, 'catch' is used with transport that you board on time, such as a bus, train or plane. The bus is something you manage to get on before it leaves.

related_collocations.example: I need to buy a ticket before I get on the bus.
Look both ways before you cross the street.
It is hard to park a car in the city centre.

memory_tip: CATCH = get on transport in time (bus, train, plane) | WATCH = look at something (film, match, TV)
